stories.headline: Ukraine targets Moscow with massive drone strike as Russian election concludes
stories.body:
Ukraine launched a massive drone attack against targets in Russia as voting ended in Russia's parliamentary election [c3]. The vote was the first parliamentary election in Russia since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022 [c3].

The political party United Russia received nearly 58 percent of the party-list vote [c1]. That total came with about 58 percent of precincts counted across the country [c1]. Official election figures showed that total voter turnout stood at 56.66 percent when the polls closed [c2].

Government authorities in Kyiv denounced voting in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine [c4]. Kyiv called the voting illegal [c4]. Ukrainian officials urged foreign governments not to recognize the election results [c4]. Russian election chief Ella Pamfilova said cyberattacks targeted Russia's electronic voting system during the election process [c6].

Russia's Defence Ministry reported that its forces shot down 1,110 Ukrainian drones across Russia, Crimea, and the Black Sea [c5]. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin gave a different figure for intercepted weapons [c7]. Sobyanin said more than 1,600 drones were intercepted and shot down in total [c7]. He said 450 of those drones were aimed at Moscow [c7].

A drone strike caused damage to a facility at the Moscow oil refinery [c9]. In the town of Sofyino, a drone struck a three-storey residential building [c10]. A 44-year-old woman was killed in Sofyino during that strike [c10]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine used domestically produced Flamingo cruise missiles to strike targets in Moscow [c8].

Attacks also took place inside Ukraine. Ukrainian officials said nine people were killed in Russian attacks in the Kyiv and Sumy regions on Saturday [c11]. Three children were among the dead in those attacks [c11].

vocab.meaning: electoral districts or voting subdivisions within a town or city
stopped or caught before reaching a destination

stories.headline: US warns citizens in Iran as military tensions rise and Houthis fire missile
stories.body:
The US Virtual Embassy in Iran issued a security alert for American citizens [c12]. The embassy urged Americans to leave Iran immediately [c12]. It told Americans to avoid travelling to Iran for any reason [c12].

US President Donald Trump said he is in a deciding mode regarding potential military action, continued economic pressure, or a deal with Iran [c14]. Officials in Tehran said Iran learned the US may be planning new strikes [c18]. Tehran warned of retaliation without limitations [c18]. Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned that all US bases and interests in the region will face continuous and painful attacks if Washington resumes military action [c15]. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said its aerospace force tracked and destroyed a US military MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz [c16].

In Saudi Arabia, coalition forces intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh [c13]. Coalition forces reported attempted attacks targeting Bish, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu [c13]. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Saudi Arabia conducted 28 air strikes targeting the governorates of Taiz, Al-Jawf, and Marib [c17]. UK Cabinet minister Bridget Phillipson said Donald Trump's war with Iran will make the UK's upcoming budget more difficult due to oil supply disruptions and inflation [c19].

vocab.meaning: action taken in return for an injury or offense
administrative divisions or provinces governed by a governor

stories.headline: German Chancellor Merz cancels UN trip following state election defeats
stories.body:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called his party's state election performance in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern a disaster [c20]. Merz said he would remain in office despite the result [c20].

In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, public broadcasters projected the far-right AfD party to win 38% of the vote [c21]. The SPD followed in second place on 35% [c21]. Merz's party, the CDU, secured 4.9 percent of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania [c25]. That result marked the party's worst state election performance in that region since 1949 [c25].

In Berlin's state election, political party Die Linke led projections with nearly 26% of the vote [c22]. The CDU placed second in Berlin on 19% [c22]. After the election losses, Merz cleared his calendar [c23]. Merz skipped a planned trip to New York for the UN General Assembly [c23].

Personal approval ratings for Merz hover just above 10 percent [c24]. Across Germany, the far-right AfD leads national opinion polls with about 30 percent support [c26].

vocab.meaning: estimated or predicted based on current data

stories.headline: US and China discuss AI safety mechanisms before White House summit
stories.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng led talks in New York [c27]. The meeting took place at JPMorgan Chase's headquarters and lasted around eight hours [c27].

The US proposed creating a US-China AI dialogue [c28]. This proposal includes a notification mechanism for high-level national security incidents resulting from AI [c28]. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said export controls on advanced AI chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment were not part of the mechanism [c30].

The talks took place before a scheduled summit meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping [c29]. The leaders are scheduled to hold a summit meeting at the White House on Thursday [c29]. A trade truce agreed by both nations in Busan, South Korea, in October 2025 is scheduled to expire on November 10 [c31].

In related developments, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called for a worldwide pacing of frontier AI development requiring cooperation with China [c32]. China released the third iteration of its AI safety governance framework [c33]. The framework addresses risks from AI agents, cybersecurity threats from frontier models, and recursive self-improvement [c33].

vocab.meaning: a new version or updated form of something
relating to a process that repeats or applies to itself

stories.headline: Delhi voter roll revision leads to widespread notices and political criticism
stories.body:
The Election Commission of India launched a voter roll review in Delhi on May 14 [c46]. The Special Intensive Revision exercise has led to millions of notices sent to voters [c34, c46]. Delhi is among 19 states and Union Territories included in the third phase of the process [c50].

Officials issued notices to 34.5% of men on Delhi's draft electoral roll [c39]. Notices went to 33.4% of women and 50% of transgender individuals on the draft roll [c39]. In total, 59,791 notices had no reason listed against them [c37].

Not being mapped to the previous review accounted for 42% of the notices issued [c34]. Name mismatches with the previous electoral roll accounted for 41% of notices [c35]. Parent name mismatches comprised 24% of notices, and self-name mismatches comprised 17% [c35]. Discrepancies in age differences accounted for 16% of notices [c36].

Prominent political and official figures received notices under the process [c42]. Served individuals included LK Advani, Jagdeep Dhankhar, S Jaishankar, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, Manish Sisodia, and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta [c42]. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta received a notice because the age difference between her and her parents appeared under 15 years [c48]. Former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B Lokur received a notice because the recorded age gap between him and his grandfather was 40 years or less [c49].

Shyam Mukhija, aged 125 from Old Delhi's Sadar Bazar assembly constituency, was the oldest person served a notice due to a self-name mismatch [c38]. Deceased former official Bibek Debroy also received a notice because his name appeared on the flagged draft rolls [c43]. Debroy was the former chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister [c43].

More than 80.62 lakh voter names were deleted from draft rolls after being marked as shifted or absent [c40]. Only 6.66 lakh Form-6 applications were submitted for inclusion [c40]. Authorities received 84,263 Form-6 applications between August 31 and September 19, after receiving 2,12,400 applications up to August 30 [c47]. In Bihar, a similar review saw the total electorate decrease from 7.89 crore to about 7.42 crore [c41]. That decrease occurred even though 21.53 lakh electors were added through Form-6 applications [c41].

Lawyer Kapil Sibal described the exercise as a special intensive deletion aimed at removing valid voters [c45]. The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office said disposal of notices will be completed by October 29, 2026 [c44]. Authorities will publish the final electoral roll on November 4, 2026 [c44].

vocab.meaning: differences or inconsistencies between facts or numbers

stories.headline: Crime Branch takes over probe into IIT Bombay student death after protests
stories.body:
Mumbai Police transferred an investigation into the death of an IIT Bombay student to the Crime Branch [c52]. An Assistant Commissioner of Police will lead the investigation [c52].

Sahil Wakode, a 20-year-old second-year student of energy science and engineering, died by suicide in his hostel room [c53, c57]. His death was the third suicide on the campus this year [c57]. An invigilating professor reported Sahil after finding him with a phone during an examination [c53]. IIT Bombay said Sahil was caught using a mobile phone to upload an exam paper onto the ChatGPT chatbot [c62].

Sahil's father filed an FIR against Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, alleging three months of harassment [c54]. Police charged Doolla and unidentified persons with abetment to suicide and violations of the SC/ST Act [c61]. Sahil's family refused to claim his body from Rajawadi Hospital for seven hours until police assured them the case went to the Crime Branch [c63].

The Faculty Forum of IIT Bombay defended Doolla, saying he executed approved exam procedures [c55]. IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare denied caste discrimination, saying student caste information remains confidential [c56]. Kedare agreed to 18 demands from protesting students, including replacing ceiling fans with wall-mounted fans in hostels [c58, c60]. Student demands included Doolla's suspension and an independent probe committee [c59].

IIT Kharagpur Director sent a message reminding students that admission serves as evidence of sustained effort [c51].

vocab.meaning: the act of encouraging or assisting someone to commit an offense
